canvas-01-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 1 is the lower right of the title sheet, at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It covers Mountain Avenue running north from the village centre, with Wilson Street entering from the west and Park Avenue leaving to the east. The west side of Mountain Avenue has small frame dwellings on lots along Wilson and Mountain Avenue, and a large vacant field behind them crossed by a diagonal lot line. The east side has a vacant field and a baseball field between Park Avenue and the lower edge, with a few dwellings, garages and sheds along the avenue and at the bottom of the part, where the street numbering continues on to sheets 2 and 3. Water pipes of four to eight inches are marked under Mountain Avenue, Wilson and Park Avenue, with hydrants. The part is separated from the key map and from the Ralston parts of the sheet by heavy lines.
notes: Wilson is Wilson Street today.
Placed from two detected junctions 39 m apart; rotation from the drawn street lines and scale from the sheet's nominal 100 ft to an inch.

Map parts: 1 bottom right, Mountain Avenue with Wilson Street and Park Avenue (north up); 2 top left, West Main Street with 3rd Street and Hamilton (2nd Street); 3 middle left, Ralston, Foundation of St. John the Baptist, upper block on West Main 1 mile SW of the fire house (turned, north about +25 deg); 4 lower left below the '660 ft omitted' break, the convent 1.5 miles SW; 5 bottom left inset, St. John Baptist School for Girls (single building).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Ralston, Foundation of St. John the Baptist, upper block on West Main 1 mile SW of the fire house (St. Anna's Cottage, pond) (no street junction drawn; West Main bends toward Chester but a trial anchor at Mendham Road / Roxiticus Road / Washington Turnpike did not match the roads or parcels; needs identification of the drawn bend, then parcel-corner control (step 6b)).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: St. John Baptist School for Girls (single building) (no street junction; one building only).

canvas-01-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 1 is the upper left of the title sheet, at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It covers West Main Street at the western end of the village, from 3rd Street to Hamilton (2nd Street), which is at the right edge, and the lots on both sides. North of West Main stand the barns, slaughter house, wagon sheds and corn crib of C. H. Day, live stock dealer, and several dwellings with barns on deep lots. South of West Main, between 3rd Street and Hamilton, are frame dwellings and a carpenter's shop on long narrow lots; 3rd Street is drawn with a dashed west edge, as an unopened or unfenced street. A water pipe runs in West Main and Hamilton. The west margin is marked no exposure, and heavy lines separate this part from the key map to the right and from the Ralston parts below.
notes: West Main is Mendham Road in OpenStreetMap (Route 24).
3rd Street is Bridge Street today; Hamilton (2nd Street) is Townsend Road.
C. H. Day, live stock dealer, is drawn north of West Main.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western half of the centre of Mendham, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left and West Main Street runs down the middle of the sheet. The sheet starts at the crossroads at the top, where Mountain Avenue, Hilltop Road and East Main Street meet West Main, and follows West Main south-westward past New Street to Hamilton (2nd Street) at the foot of the sheet. The block between Mountain Avenue and New Street, on the north-west side of West Main, is the commercial core of the village: the Black Horse Inn on Mountain Avenue, club rooms, a tinware, hardware and plumbing shop, several automobile repair shops and storage garages, the Charles Freeman Block, and the Mendham Fire Department Station No. 1 with the Mendham Garage Co., beside a hall used for storing scenery. A private alley leads west from West Main behind the shop of J. M. Hoffman, mason, contractor and builder. On the south-east side, St. Joseph's R.C. Church stands back from the street behind a looping drive, with its rectory and a large grave yard. South of New Street are the yard and sash and door storage of E. L. Garrabrant, builder, and the greenhouses of John H. Quimby, florist, among frame dwellings on deep lots. The remainder of the sheet is detached frame dwellings with barns, sheds and stables. Water pipes of four to eight inches run under West Main, New Street and Hamilton, with hydrants marked along them. Vacant fields lie at the south-east edge.
notes: West Main and East Main are Mendham Road in OpenStreetMap (Route 24; addresses West and East Main Street).
Hamilton (2nd Street) is Townsend Road today.
New is New Street today.
St. Joseph's R.C. Church and grave yard, Black Horse Inn and Mendham Fire Department Station No. 1 are drawn.

50 ft to an inch, north to the left (about -75 deg). West Main Street from the Mountain Avenue / Hilltop Road crossroads to Hamilton (2nd Street); New Street, Black Horse Inn, St. Joseph's R.C. Church, fire station. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 3 is the main map of the sheet, at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the left. It covers East Main Street from the crossroads with Mountain Avenue and Hilltop Road at the foot of the sheet north-eastward to Orchard Street at the top, with the lots along both sides and the north side of Orchard Street. East Main is the village's civic street: from the crossroads it passes a row of stores with a drug store, a hardware store and a plumbing shop, the post office on the corner of Hilltop Road, St. Mark's Episcopal Church with its rectory, the public library, the M. E. Church with its parsonage and a long row of auto sheds behind it, and the Town Hall. At the corner of Orchard Street stands the cement-floored garage of J. Smith Gunther, auto sales and repair. A lane leads east from East Main toward the east edge. Behind the East Main frontage the west side of the sheet is vacant fields, and the north side of Orchard Street is lined with small frame dwellings. A short stretch of Mountain Avenue with a few dwellings is drawn along the lower left. A boxed inset of another stretch of Mountain Avenue, further north, occupies the left side of the sheet and is a separate part. Water pipes of four to eight inches are marked in East Main, Orchard Street, Mountain Avenue and Hilltop Road.
notes: East Main is Mendham Road in OpenStreetMap (Route 24; addresses East Main Street).
Orchard is Orchard Street today.
Town Hall, post office, public library, M. E. Church and St. Mark's Episcopal Church are drawn.
The lane east of East Main has no modern counterpart found.

50 ft to an inch, north about -60 deg. East Main Street from the crossroads to Orchard Street, Town Hall, M.E. Church, post office. Part 1 main map; part 2 inset (left, heavy line box), Mountain Avenue far north of town with a brook and the Charles Q. Garrabrant property, block 14.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Mountain Avenue north of the village, brook and Charles Q. Garrabrant property, block 14 (no street junction drawn; needs parcel-corner control along Mountain Avenue (step 6b)).

sheet-4-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 4 is the lower and larger part of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the right. It covers East Main Street east of Orchard Street, which enters at the left edge, through the eastern end of the village. North of East Main are deep lots with dwellings, barns and outbuildings, the Adams Poultry Farm reached by a lane from the north, the carpenter shop of C. D. Carley, and further east a lane leading north past a dog kennel. South of East Main the west end has a dense row of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, numbered 424 to 437; east of them the land opens into the W. C. Cullen Farm, whose farm buildings, barn yard, ice house and a stone building stand near the foot of the sheet beside a 20 foot lane. The diagonal boundary of the Franklin Murphy Property crosses the lower right corner. A heavy line separates this part from part 2 above it, and the margins along it and the right edge are marked no exposure. A water pipe runs in East Main and one branches south toward the Cullen farm, with hydrants marked. The rest of the area is fields and scattered dwellings.
notes: East Main is Mendham Road in OpenStreetMap (Route 24).
Orchard is Orchard Street today; the junction with East Main is at the left edge.
The lane to the Adams Poultry Farm lies near the line of today's Hillcrest Avenue but is drawn as a farm lane not reaching East Main.

100 ft to an inch. Part 1 (lower, larger): East Main Street east of Orchard Street, Adams Poultry Farm, W. C. Cullen Farm, turned (north about +35 deg). Part 2 (upper): Prospect Street, New Street, Hilltop Road and Talmadge Road, Presbyterian church, high school; north up.

sheet-4-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 4 is the upper part of the sheet, at 100 feet to an inch with north up. It covers the area south of the village centre between New Street and Hilltop Road: Prospect Street running east from New Street to Hilltop Road, and Hilltop Road running south from the top edge past the Presbyterian church to its fork with Talmadge Road. The short end of 2d Street appears at the top left. Prospect Street is lined with frame dwellings, several with stables and garages, and a long driveway loops through the large lots west of New Street. East of Hilltop Road stand the high school, a steel-framed building with a gymnasium and hall and a cooking school, the Presbyterian manse, and the Presbyterian church with its spire, a row of auto sheds along Talmadge Road and a grave yard behind. Below the fork Hilltop Road curves away south-west across vacant fields. A small dashed island is drawn where Talmadge Road leaves Hilltop Road. Water pipes are marked in New Street, Prospect Street, Hilltop Road and Talmadge Road. A heavy line separates this part from part 1 below it.
notes: Prospect is Prospect Street, New is New Street today.
2d Street is the end of Hamilton (2nd Street), today Townsend Road.
The high school and the Presbyterian church, manse and grave yard are drawn.
Talmadge Road leaves Hilltop Road in two legs around a small island, as OpenStreetMap still has it.

100 ft to an inch. Part 1 (lower, larger): East Main Street east of Orchard Street, Adams Poultry Farm, W. C. Cullen Farm, turned (north about +35 deg). Part 2 (upper): Prospect Street, New Street, Hilltop Road and Talmadge Road, Presbyterian church, high school; north up.
